info.title: Material KAI — Supabase Edge Functions
info.description:
OpenAPI for the **Supabase Edge Functions** (Deno/TypeScript) of the Material KAI Vision Platform.

This is the companion to the FastAPI-generated `openapi.json` at `https://v1api.materialshub.gr/openapi.json`, which covers the **MIVAA Python** backend only. Edge functions are a separate runtime with no auto-generated schema, so this spec is **hand-maintained** from the source code (`scripts/edge-endpoints.json` → `scripts/build-openapi-edge.mjs`).

Most functions are **action-based**: POST a JSON body with an `action` field; the spec models each action as a discriminated `oneOf` branch. Finance/REST-style functions use typed bodies or path/method routing (see each operation's description). Auth varies per function — see `security` and the scheme descriptions.

Stateful LLM chat endpoint supporting three agents (kai, interior-designer, demo). Uses LangGraph StateGraph for multi-step tool execution. Supports multimodal input (data-URL images), long-term memory, toolkit-based tool selection, and optional partner API key access. Returns SSE stream of JSON chunks; content-type text/event-stream.

post.summary: Every-minute cron: dispatch background agents whose cron schedule is due
post.description:
Runs every minute via pg_cron. Evaluates all enabled background_agents with trigger_type='cron', parses their cron expression, and dispatches due agents to background-agent-runner. Includes concurrency guard to skip agents with an in-flight run.

**Response:** `{ success, checked, triggered, results: [{ agent_id, name, triggered, run_id?, error? }] }`

post.summary: Weekly cron (Sunday 00:00 UTC): sync AI model prices from hardcoded reference tables
post.description:
Reads ai_model_pricing rows with auto_update_enabled=true, compares current prices against a hardcoded per-provider reference (Anthropic, OpenAI, Voyage, Google, Firecrawl), updates changed rows, and writes an audit row to ai_pricing_update_logs. Accepts optional POST body to force-update or filter by provider.

**Response:** `{ success, message, stats: { models_checked, models_updated, models_skipped, models_failed, results }, timestamp }`

post.summary: Reorder search results by relevance to a query
post.description:
Cross-encoder style reranking over candidates the caller already holds. Fuses the platform's six per-aspect embedding scores (visual/colour/texture/style/material/understanding) into one ordering using claude-haiku-4-5. Degrades to the SOURCE ORDER on every failure path - fewer than 2 candidates, no API key, model error, or a model reply naming ids that were not sent - and reports which happened in `reranked`/`reason`, so a caller never mistakes an unranked list for a ranked one. Ranks by id rather than index, so a shifted candidate list cannot silently reorder the wrong results. The same logic runs in-process for the agent's material_search, visual_search and knowledge_base_search tools; this endpoint is for callers outside the agent runtime. Prompt is editable at /admin/ai-configs (prompts.category='ai_rerank').

**Response:** `{results:[...], reranked:boolean, reason?:string, explanations?:{[id]:string}, model:string}`

results.description: Candidates to reorder (max 200; only the first 40 are ranked). Each: {id, name, description?, category?, relevanceScore?, semanticScore?, understandingScore?}

maxResults.description: Truncate AFTER reranking, so the model still sees the full set

includeExplanations.description: Return a one-line rationale per result (default false)

post.summary: Every-5-minute cron: detect and recover stuck PDF, XML, scraping, and agent runs
post.description:
Scans background_jobs, scraping_sessions, and agent_runs for heartbeat-stale entries. Atomically claims each and re-dispatches to MIVAA or background-agent-runner. Terminally-failed exhausted PDF jobs are marked failed and HuggingFace endpoints are scaled to zero as a cost watchdog.

**Response:** `{ success, totalStuck, exhausted_failed, recovered, failed, results }`

post.summary: Bulk facet re-canonicalization sweep (proxy to MIVAA)
post.description:
Internal-only proxy to MIVAA's POST /api/admin/facets/recanonicalize (#316). Replays products.attributes_raw through the canonicalizer so a similarity-threshold change, a curated alias, or an outage-degraded product can be repaired without re-ingesting any source PDF. Driven nightly at 03:40 by the facets-recanonicalize-degraded cron with degraded_only=true; a full catalog re-sweep costs a Voyage embedding per raw value and must be requested explicitly. Requires service-role or x-cron-secret (isCronAuthorized) — an open proxy here would be an open Voyage spend. Returns `remaining` so the caller knows whether to run again.

**Response:** (`application/json`)

Now mode (admin JWT): sends an on-demand digest for a specific workspace.

post.summary: Pull inbound documents from myDATA (RequestDocs) for configured workspaces
post.description:
Polls the AADE myDATA RequestDocs endpoint for each workspace that has configured inbound credentials, upserts received documents into inbound_documents, and advances the per-workspace MARK watermark. The manual 'Sync from myDATA' path may bound the pull to an issue-date window (date_from/date_to) so a sync doesn't drag in years of history. Cron path charges 2 credits per workspace; manual 'Sync now' (JWT) is free. No-ops cleanly when credentials are absent.

**Response:** `{ok, workspaces, results: [{workspaceId, found, upserted, new_watermark, date_from?, date_to?} | {workspaceId, skipped|error}]}`

date_from.description: Manual path only. Start of the issue-date window to pull. Must be sent together with date_to and be <= it; sent to AADE as dateFrom in dd/MM/yyyy. Omit both to pull from the stored MARK watermark. (string (yyyy-mm-dd))

get.summary: Public product + 3D model read for the website embed SDK
get.description:
Anonymous read API for the <materialkai-product> embed (#321 M1 / #258). Authenticated by a publishable embed key (material_kai_keys) sent as the x-embed-key header or ?key= query param; the key resolves the workspace, so no caller-supplied workspace id is ever trusted. The key's allowed_origins drives per-request CORS (browser-enforced) and its rate_limit_per_minute is consumed atomically per call. Serves only products with a storefront-published price row — the same publication gate as the online storefront. Each key additionally carries a catalog scope (all | categories | products) enforced server-side on BOTH actions: a scoped key naming an out-of-scope product_id gets the same 404 as another tenant's id, and request params can only narrow the scope, never widen it.

📖 [docs/blueprint-estimating.md](https://github.com/creativeghq/material-kai-vision-platform/blob/main/docs/blueprint-estimating.md)

post.summary: Google Search Console for connected websites (OAuth + performance sync)
post.description:
Connects a user_website to a Google Search Console property and pulls first-party search-analytics (query/page/clicks/impressions/ctr/position) into gsc_performance. OAuth is SERVER-SIDE: Google's redirect_uri points at THIS function (GET ?code&state); it exchanges the code and 302s back to /profile?tab=websites&gsc=<connected|pick_property|error>. This avoids the SPA's supabase-js (detectSessionInUrl+PKCE) intercepting Google's ?code= as a login code. `state` is an HMAC-signed {website_id,user_id,ts} minted at authorize-time after authenticate()+userCanAccessWorkspace(). Tokens live in website_gsc_connections (service-role only). verify_jwt disabled so the GET callback + cron (x-cron-secret, action=cron-sync) work.

**Routes / actions:**
- `GET ?code&state` — Google's server-side redirect target. Verifies the signed state, exchanges the code, stores the connection, auto-matches the property + backfills 28 days, then 302s to the app. No JSON body.
- `authorize` — Return the Google consent URL for a website (signed state binds the server-side callback to this website + user).
- `list_properties` — List the GSC properties the connected Google account can access.
- `set_property` — Bind a specific GSC property to the website when auto-match didn't.
- `sync` — Pull the last N days of search-analytics now (default 28).
- `disconnect` — Deactivate and clear the stored tokens (history is kept).
- `cron-sync` — x-cron-secret only — nightly refresh of every active connection + 180-day retention prune.

post.summary: Viva event delivery (1796 / 1797 / 1798 / 2054)
post.description:
#273 Phase 2 - Viva.com webhooks, multi-tenant BYOK. Two surfaces:

- GET  - the verification-key handshake Viva performs at webhook registration. The key is per-merchant, so the caller passes ?workspace_id=<uuid> to say which tenant is registering; the function fetches that workspace's key from Viva and echoes it back.
- POST - the event deliveries: 1796 payment created, 1797 reversal created, 1798 payment failed, 2054 account transaction (merchant-level, covers incoming RF bank transfers).

SECURITY: Viva payment webhooks carry NO per-message signature (Viva-Signature-256 exists only on their Data Services contract, which has a shared secret; payment webhooks have none), so there is nothing to verify per delivery. Invariant #6 is satisfied differently and more strongly: THE WEBHOOK IS A TRIGGER, NEVER DATA - the handler reads the transaction back from Viva's API and acts on that, so a forged delivery cannot inject state. Settled 1796/RF payments are mirrored into the unified bank feed (provider viva, informational).

**Response:** `{ ok } (always 200 to Viva once accepted; processing errors are logged, not surfaced)`

Runs a workspace's saved Viva credentials against Viva for real and returns a per-step verdict: the Smart Checkout OAuth pair, the Merchant pair (the same call the webhook verification handshake makes), creating a payment order on the configured source, and reading that order back.

WHY IT EXISTS: every field on the Viva setup card is silently wrong until a customer pays. A mistyped payment source code — Viva issues a 4-DIGIT code per source — authenticates, saves, and is accepted by every layer right up until the first real sale. The order read-back is the only check that proves it, because Viva echoes SourceCode back.

No money moves: the test order is 0.30, nobody is redirected to checkout, and paymentTimeout expires it in five minutes. The webhook leg is NOT testable here (Viva offers no way to trigger a delivery) — `workspace_viva_config.webhook_event_types` records what actually arrives instead.

TENANCY: caller must be a finance manager of the target workspace, checked under their own RLS via supabaseAsUser; mismatch returns 404, not 403.

post.description:
The unauthenticated half of Real Estate — deliberately a separate function from `real-estate-api` so no authed surface is reachable without a session. **Response:** `{ listing | listings | buyer | estimate | ok } | { error } — toPublic() projection only`

get.summary: Pushes viewings into the agent's own Google Calendar (per-user OAuth)
get.description:
Viewings already sync to the platform calendar (`crm_meetings`); what an agent lives in is Google Calendar on their phone, and a viewing they cannot see there is one they miss. Reuses the platform GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET and the token/refresh shape already proven in `gsc-api`, so Google is configured once rather than once per feature. Actions: `status`, `connect` (returns the consent URL), `disconnect`, `push-viewing`. The GET path is Google's OAuth callback. The connection is per USER and its RLS is owner-only — it holds one person's tokens and workspace membership deliberately grants nothing. `state` is HMAC-signed with the service key and carries user + workspace, so the callback cannot be replayed to bind someone else's Google account; `prompt=consent` forces a refresh_token even on reconnect, without which a stored connection dies within the hour. `push-viewing` re-checks the caller may see the viewing before writing to any calendar, cancels the Google event when the viewing is cancelled, and records `last_sync_error` rather than swallowing it — a calendar that silently stops syncing looks exactly like one with no viewings.

**Response:** `{ connected, google_email, last_sync_at, last_sync_error, configured } | { auth_url } | { ok, event_id }`

get.summary: Short-let channel sync — availability feed out (GET, token) and channel calendars in (POST, cron)
get.description:
Booking channels all speak iCalendar and nothing else, so this one function is the whole integration. **GET ?token=…** serves the availability feed a channel pulls, authorised solely by the per-listing `ical_token`; it publishes BLOCKED NIGHTS ONLY — no guest name, email or price — because that URL is a bearer capability handed to third parties. **POST** (shared cron gate) pulls every active `property_channel_links.ical_import_url`, re-validating each through the shared SSRF guard at read time as well as write time, and upserts on `(property, channel, UID)` so a channel republishing its whole calendar every poll does not duplicate every stay. A `23P01` exclusion violation on import is reported as a date conflict rather than swallowed — that IS a double booking, and only the operator can resolve it on the channel that sold it twice. Runs hourly.

**Response:** `text/calendar (GET) | { ok, links, imported, conflicts, failed } (POST)`

post.summary: Public tokenised endpoint — turns a forwarded portal enquiry email into a CRM lead
post.description:
Syndication pushes listings out; the enquiries portals generate come back as email. An agency points any inbound-email service (Resend, Mailgun routes, SendGrid Inbound Parse, Cloudflare Email Workers) at this URL and forwards portal mail to it. The per-workspace `inbound_lead_token` IS the credential and is checked BEFORE anything is parsed or written — the From address is spoofable and is used only to guess which portal sent it. Fails closed: unknown token or ingestion disabled both return the same 401, so probing cannot confirm a valid token. `workspace_id` comes from the token and `property_id` from the listing's own `reference_code`; nothing identifying is taken from the payload. Parses name / email / phone / reference / message, skipping the portal's own no-reply address, routes the lead through `route_property_lead`, and keeps the parsed source in `inbound_raw` because portal formats change silently. A message with no contactable details returns 200 (a digest or receipt must not be retried forever).

post.summary: Unified monitoring dispatcher — one function behind all five price / mention / job cron tasks
post.description:
Replaces the five near-identical monitoring crons (`price-monitoring-cron`, `mention-monitoring-cron`, `llm-mention-probe-cron`, `job-research-cron`, `job-research-digest-cron`). Each was the same boilerplate — cron-secret check → module gate → POST to a MIVAA cron endpoint — differing only in module slug and path.

pg_cron passes `?task=<task>`. The task gates on its own module toggle (a disabled module returns `{skipped:'module_disabled'}` rather than running a paid refresh) and then delegates to MIVAA, which selects the due rows and processes them in batch. Auth is the shared cron gate: `x-cron-secret` **or** a service-role bearer, so a vault/env secret-name drift can no longer 401 all five tasks at once.

External API consumers (`api_key_id IS NOT NULL`) are intentionally never touched by the refresh tasks — they pay per call and control their own cadence.

The keep-active link resolves through the public `moodboard-keep-active` function. Backed by the `moodboard_dormancy_scan` RPC. Note that moodboards are **user**-scoped, not workspace-scoped, so notification targeting is per-owner.

post.summary: Revolut Business connection management (per-workspace BYOK) — keys, OAuth, accounts, mapping, sync
post.description:
#315. Actions on one POST surface: init (mint RSA keypair server-side; private key never leaves the server), authorize-url (Revolut consent URL), oauth-complete (exchange the auth code via JWT client assertion), register-webhook (webhooks v2 subscription + signing secret), accounts (live Revolut accounts + finance_bank_accounts mapping), map-account (link a Revolut currency pocket to a bank account row), sync-now (shared sync core for this workspace), disconnect. Caller must be a finance manager of the target workspace (RLS-checked; 404 on mismatch) and the workspace must be entitled to banking-revolut (402 otherwise). validate-account-name proxies Revolut CoP/VoP so the CRM bank area can confirm an IBAN belongs to the named counterparty; map-account auto-fills the finance row IBAN/BIC from /accounts/{id}/bank-details when empty. Phase 2 adds reconciliation: reconcile re-runs the invoice matcher; confirm-match settles a statement line against an invoice through record-payment; ignore-transaction parks a line. Phase 3 adds money-out: create-counterparty mirrors a CRM bank row as a Revolut counterparty (VoP-gated; not_matched blocks unless force=true); send-payment creates a draft (human approves in-app) or a direct transfer; create-payout-link pays without an IBAN; fx-rate/exchange convert between pockets. Every instruction is audited in revolut_payouts with an idempotent request_id before Revolut is called. Phase 4 adds team cards (issue virtual, freeze/unfreeze) and card-expense browsing with on-demand receipt passthrough (never persisted). import-expenses attributes card expenses to employees (card→holder email→HR roster) into monthly expense reports with receipts; also runs with the cron sweep, which additionally freezes cards of offboarded employees. pay-due-bills drafts ONE multi-payment run over due supplier_bills (suppliers without a VoP-linked counterparty are skipped and reported); set-card-limit patches weekly/monthly spending caps; create-card-invitation invites a new member by email. sync-labels pushes platform finance categories into a "Platform categories" Revolut label group (names only, never deletes). reconcile also settles OUTGOING transfers against supplier_bills (reference-quotes-bill-number or exact-amount+supplier-name; payments direction out + payment_allocations.supplier_bill_id). confirm-bill-match manually settles an OUTGOING revolut feed line against a supplier bill. The feed table is now multi-provider (revolut|stripe|viva); stripe/viva rows are informational mirrors of webhook-settled money and are guarded against re-matching.

**Response:** `{ok: true, ...action-specific fields (public_key, url, accounts, fetched/upserted)}`

post.summary: Deliver queued outbound webhook events to tenant endpoints
post.description:
Cron function that POSTs queued deliveries to tenant endpoints (#330). Signs each request HMAC-SHA256 over '{timestamp}.{body}' and sends it as X-MaterialKai-Signature, with the timestamp inside the signed string so a captured delivery cannot be replayed later. Re-runs the shared SSRF guard at delivery time (not just at registration - DNS behind a stored hostname can be re-pointed) and refuses to follow redirects. Retries with exponential backoff to a hard attempt cap; an SSRF rejection fails immediately rather than retrying. An endpoint that fails enough consecutive deliveries is auto-disabled.

post.summary: Installed base: a customer's equipment, its warranties and its recurring service schedules (#343).
post.description:
Action-discriminated JWT endpoint over customer_assets, customer_asset_warranties, customer_asset_service_plans and customer_asset_service_events, plus the per-product defaults in product_service_defaults. Reads and writes run through the caller's own RLS context; registration and service completion go through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs that call assert_workspace_member. There is no next_due_on field anywhere: the next due date IS the plan's single open service event, served by the customer_asset_service_due view. Ownership mismatches return 404, never 403. Warranty certificates upload through this function (service-role write to the private pdf-documents bucket under warranties/, after ownership is proven on the RLS-bound client) and are read via a short-lived signed URL; the row stores bucket + path and never a URL. Deleting an asset that has logged service returns 409 - the DB refuses it so the history cannot be erased.

post.summary: Cron: emit equipment service-due, service-overdue and warranty-expiring flow events (#343).
post.description:
Runs daily via pg_cron (x-cron-secret via isCronAuthorized). Scans the customer_asset_service_due view for open occurrences inside their lead-time window and customer_asset_warranties approaching ends_on, then emits asset.service_due, asset.service_overdue and asset.warranty_expiring flow events with the recipient resolved from the plan assignee, the customer's responsible sales users, or the workspace owners/admins. It never writes a user_notifications row or calls email-api directly — the seeded system-default flows deliver. Each reminder is stamped on its row so it fires once, and only after the emit actually succeeded; a transient failure leaves the row unstamped for the next tick. Backed by the ops.asset_reminders_silent_zero integrity probe.

**Response:** `{ success, scanned_due, scanned_warranties, serviceDue, serviceOverdue, warrantyExpiring, failed }`
